competitors.title: Awesome Agent Skills -- Claude Code, Codex & Cursor Skills Directory
key_points: Presents itself as a living index of reusable agent skills for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and other emerging platforms
Frames the directory as a curated atlas rather than a raw dump of links, which makes curation and discoverability part of the product
Explains agent skills in simple terms for newcomers and gives a direct install path for Claude Code skills
Signals the same cross-platform positioning VoltAgent is aiming for, so it is a direct SERP competitor

competitors.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
key_points: Defines skills as folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents can discover and load dynamically
Makes progressive disclosure the core design principle, which is the mental model most readers need before using a skills directory
Shows the SKILL.md format and how bundled files deepen the capability without bloating the initial prompt
Functions as the canonical explanation of the standard that many community directories now build around

competitors.title: Agent Skills - Codex | OpenAI Developers
key_points: Positions skills as reusable task-specific capabilities with instructions, resources, and optional scripts
Reinforces progressive disclosure and explicit vs implicit triggering, which is central to how people evaluate skills
Connects skills to a broader Codex workflow story rather than a one-off install list
Competes for readers who want a platform-native skills reference instead of a third-party directory

competitors.title: Spring AI Agentic Patterns (Part 1): Agent Skills - Modular, Reusable Capabilities
key_points: Reframes agent skills as LLM-agnostic modular capabilities that can run with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or other supported models
Highlights the SKILL.md folder structure with scripts, references, and assets, which closely mirrors how directories like VoltAgent's repo are organized
Gives Java developers an implementation path, so it competes on portability and ecosystem reach
Pairs skills with other agentic patterns, which makes the article attractive to readers who want broader architecture guidance

competitors.title: AI Agent Skills: The New Standard for Modular AI Workflows
key_points: Frames skills as modular workflow units that can be reused across agents and environments
Introduces the security and governance angle early, which matters for anyone deciding whether to trust a public directory
Mentions a free Skills Security Scanner, so it competes on evaluation and trust, not just discovery
Targets teams that care about policy and risk controls as much as convenience

competitors.title: Learn How to Write Effective Agent Skills
key_points: Acts as a beginner-friendly how-to for writing SKILL.md files without code
Explains progressive disclosure using a simple three-level model that newcomers can apply immediately
Focuses on small workflows, testing with real requests, and iterating on descriptions for better triggering
Competes for search traffic from readers who are learning skills before they are ready to browse a directory

stats.fact: VoltAgent's awesome-agent-skills repository is positioned as a curated collection of 1000+ agent skills.
The same repository page reports about 27.2k stars, 2.9k forks, and 93 contributors in July 2026.
Anthropic published Agent Skills as an open standard on December 18, 2025.
stats.source: Anthropic engineering post on Agent Skills

stats.fact: OpenAI's Codex skills docs say the initial skills list uses at most 2% of the model context window, or 8,000 characters when the window is unknown.
Spring AI says its Agent Skills implementation is LLM-agnostic and works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or other supported models.
stats.source: Spring AI Agentic Patterns (Part 1): Agent Skills

stats.fact: Google's official skills repository is installable with `npx skills install github.com/google/skills` and is meant to work across Antigravity, Gemini CLI, and third-party agents.
stats.source: Google Cloud blog on official skills repository
